title: VCF-RDFizer evaluation: benchmark harness, run records, and figure sources
description:
The evaluation of VCF-RDFizer reported in VCF-RDFizer: From a VCF File to Explicit, Verifiable, and Policy-aware Semantic Genomic Data: every number, table, and figure in the manuscript and its supplement can be traced to a run record in this archive and regenerated from it.

Contents

  • benchmarks/: the benchmark harness (experiments 00-17, including the linked workflow in benchmarks/use_case/acmg/). The drivers that ran it on each benchmark host are archived with their run records.
  • BioMedSem_2026/benchmark-results/: the run records of every reported run, per host: commands, tool commits, image digests, timings, resource samples, validation reports, query results, comparisons, and logs. Generated graphs and indexes are not included.
  • BioMedSem_2026/paper-assets/ and scripts/build_site_data.py: the figure and results-site scripts, which read only the run records (python3 BioMedSem_2026/paper-assets/figures/make_figures.py).
  • BioMedSem_2026/paper/: the manuscript and supplement sources.
  • Inputs: the download command for every input VCF (README.md), their SHA-256 checksums (BioMedSem_2026/benchmark-results/input-checksums.tsv and vcf-input-sizes.json), and the scripts that derive the evaluated slices.

Software: the base benchmark campaign ran VCF-RDFizer v3.1.0 (image ecrum19/vcf-rdfizer@sha256:1904e96dde12ab2e2e70d8ee1267765c293ab100a8bd1b14d5b009b2bf8e34aa); the linked workflow, the retrieval experiments, and the consumer WGS validation run used VCF-RDFizer v3.3.1 (image ecrum19/vcf-rdfizer@sha256:3ad71b1a54612142e3be43b24e7e4a38551949cb641f4421bcae9bf051102993). The two releases write identical graphs: their conversions of the 100,000-record HG005 slice have the same 17,098,746 triples (sorted N-Triples SHA-256 661578e7…94ed).

Not included: the source VCFs, which remain available from their providers (Genome in a Bottle, the 1000 Genomes Project, HGSVC2, precisionFDA, and the Personal Genome Project); the generated RDF graphs and indexes, which the archived commands regenerate; and the Docker images, which are pulled by digest.
